Q: Read and display milliseconds A:

%S is for integer seconds, %OS is for partial seconds. You only need one or the other. And no need to set options(), just use:

library(readr)

parse_time(c("03:44:43.300 PM", "03:44:43.301 PM"), "%I:%M:%OS %p")
#15:44:43.300
#15:44:43.301

I added a second time string for illustrative purposes as readr drops trailing zeros by default. That's because readr uses strptime() {base} (thanks @JonSpring):

Specific to R is %OSn, which for output gives the seconds truncated to exactly 0 <= n <= 6 decimal places. If %OS is not followed by a digit, it uses up to digits decimals (only as many as necessary, i.e., not producing extra trailing zeros. The default digits = NULL corresponds to digits = 0.

Note that although readr uses strptime(), as @margusl pointed out it comes with its own parser implementation, which:

uses a format specification similar to strptime()

See also readrDateTimeParser.h.

Q: Placing characters at a specific column in vi A:

You can add two horizontal lines and some spaces as following:

:%s/^/  
:%s/\_.*/-\r&-
:%g/-/norm gn20A-
:%g/.*/normal 20A

Then sorround it by ! characters at desired column number (for example \%>17c):

:%s/^\|\%>17c.*/!/g

Another way using keybindings:

iEnterEsc

Ctrl+vGI Esc

k25I-EscyyGp

ggCtrl+vGI!Esc

Ctrl+vG$15A Esc

18lCtrl+vG$c!Esc

Q: Codeigniter my helper function A:

Calling a helper function in view can be done, but better way as per the convention would be to call it in controller and pass it to view form controller. like:

$data['someVar'] = city_accent($e->city);
$this->load->view("your_view", $data);

Hope it helps

Q: How can I load model to helper? A:

This is an XY Problem. Stop and refactor.

A helper file is a collection of globally-scoped function declarations. These functions exist outside of the Model-View-Controller (MVC) architecture.

All helper functions should:

  • be completely ignorant of the source (a layer of MVC, user submission, session, cookie, etc.) of their input data (this makes unit testing simpler and improves the re-usability of helper functions);
  • not contain business logic;
  • never need to call out to other layers of the MVC architecture;
  • never need to directly interact with the database or filesystem;
  • typically be used for data mutation or presentation;

When you start to see business logic creep into your helper functions, it is likely that your process should be abstracted to a context specific library, or perhaps become a private or protected method within your controller or model. Libraries are a fantastic place to write context/business-specific processes. Libraries extend from controllers and your IDE (e.g. PhpStorm) will have an easier time providing Ctrl-click navigation to other layers in the MVC.

Although the hack of declaring $CI = get_instance(); then loading a model with $CI->load->model('Your_model'); works, it is an antipattern.

There's nothing wrong with having mundane tasks with no contextual relevance performed by helper functions, just make sure that all required data is passed in as arguments. Simple. Clean. No MVC hacking.

Q: How can I show file sizes with commas when getting a directory listing with 'ls -l'? A:

There is now an answer in macOS:

ls -l -,

or

ls -l,
